practiceSet.title: U1.LT3 Practice: Dimensional Analysis & Scientific Notation
practiceSet.description: Practice converting units with the 5 steps and writing numbers in scientific notation; use the Unit Relationships given in each question.

activity.title: U1.LT3 Relearning: Dimensional Analysis & Scientific Notation
activity.content:
**What you need to be able to do:** I can convert numbers into different units (dimensional analysis) and use scientific notation.

**Think of it like trading money.** Four quarters and one dollar are the same amount of money, just counted in different units. When you trade 8 quarters for dollars, you know 4 quarters = 1 dollar, so you get 2 dollars. You did not gain or lose money; only the unit changed. Converting units works the same way.

**Dimensional analysis** is a way to change from one set of units to another. A **Unit Relationship** is the amount of one unit being equal to another, like 1 ft = 12 in. A **conversion factor** is that relationship written as a fraction, like 12 in / 1 ft. Because the top and bottom are the same amount, a conversion factor is **equal to one**, so multiplying by it changes the units but not the amount. Use the reference sheet for the Unit Relationships; you do not have to memorize them. Exact numbers like 12 in = 1 ft have infinite sig figs, so they never limit your answer.

**The 5 steps:** 1) **Identify**: given units on the left, wanted units on the right. 2) **Conversion Factors**: find the Unit Relationship. 3) **Set Up**: insert factors so units cancel (**Top vs Bottom**: the unit you have goes on the bottom of the factor; for a rate like ft/s, the s is already on the bottom of the given, so it goes on top of its factor). 4) **Calculate**: multiply the tops and divide by the bottoms. 5) **Sig Figs and Label**: no naked numbers!

**Scientific notation** is digits with a decimal point after the first digit, followed by × 10 to a power. The exponent is **+** if you started with a big number (bigger than 1) and **−** if you started with a small number (less than 1). Keep the same sig figs: 101,000 = 1.01 × 10^{5}.

**Worked example 1:** Convert 3.40 lb to kg. Unit Relationship: 1 kg = 2.205 lb. Set Up: 3.40 lb × (1 kg / 2.205 lb). Lb is on the bottom, so it cancels. Calculate: 3.40 ÷ 2.205 = 1.542. Sig Figs and Label: 3.40 has 3 sig figs, so the answer is **1.54 kg**.

**Worked example 2:** Convert 1.50 ft to cm. There is no ft = cm relationship, so plan a chain: ft → in → cm. Set Up: 1.50 ft × (12 in / 1 ft) × (2.54 cm / 1 in). Feet cancel, then inches cancel. Calculate: 1.50 × 12 × 2.54 = 45.72. Answer: **45.7 cm**.

**Worked example 3:** Write 0.000752 in scientific notation. Move the decimal 4 places to the right to get 7.52. The starting number is small, so the exponent is negative: **7.52 × 10^{-4}**. Going the other way, 6.1 × 10^{3} has a positive exponent, so move the decimal 3 places right: **6,100**.

**Watch out for:** flipping the conversion factor (if the unit you started with is on top, it will not cancel); dividing when you should multiply; giving the wrong sign on the exponent; and leaving off the unit or copying every digit from the calculator.
prompts: Convert 5.8 kg to lb. Write the Unit Relationship (1 kg = 2.205 lb) first, then show your setup, your answer, and the unit.
Convert 2.0 gal to cups using 1 gal = 4 qt and 1 qt = 4 cups. Show the picket fence and explain how you knew which unit went on the bottom of each factor.
Write 0.00419 in scientific notation and explain how you knew whether the exponent is positive or negative.
Write 8.2 × 10^{5} in standard notation. Explain which way you moved the decimal and why.
